analysis.investment_thesis: Jubilant Pharmova is a complex six-segment pharmaceutical conglomerate that has delivered essentially zero revenue growth over nine years (2.6% CAGR) and negative EBITDA growth (-3.1% CAGR), with ROE and ROCE both stuck below 10%. The 2025 net profit of 836 Cr looks impressive until you strip out the 416 Cr of 'other income' — the operating business earned only ~420 Cr, making the 31x P/E look far more expensive than it appears.
key_strengths: Radiopharma segment has genuine niche positioning in nuclear medicine with high barriers to entry
Debt/Equity of 0.44 has improved from peak leverage (4,808 Cr borrowings in 2020 vs. 2,883 Cr today)
Operating cash flow positive in all 5 years of data provided
key_risks: Revenue of 7,234 Cr in 2025 barely exceeds the 7,518 Cr earned in 2018 — a lost decade of growth
CWIP at 2,344 Cr signals massive ongoing capex with FCF that is negative or near-zero in recent years
Earnings quality is poor: 2025 net profit heavily dependent on 416 Cr 'other income'; core operating margin just 7.95%
red_flags: Net loss of 65 Cr in 2023 and only 73 Cr profit in 2024 — the business has been structurally impaired
Six disparate business segments signal complexity and lack of focus — I prefer businesses a child can understand
Free cash flow was negative or near-zero in 2023, 2024, and 2025 despite heavy capital investment totaling 2,400+ Cr
analysis.detailed_analysis: I look for businesses that compound capital at high rates over long periods. Jubilant Pharmova has done the opposite — EBITDA was actually higher in 2016 (1,603 Cr) than in 2025 (1,212 Cr). The company has invested heavily in capacity and diversification and gotten worse financial results. That is a capital allocation failure. The radiopharma business is genuinely interesting, but it is buried inside a conglomerate that dilutes its returns.
